messages.subject: Modelling behavioral response
messages.body_plain:
Hi group,

I have an issue concerning modelling behavioral response with my white-tailed deer encounter history data.

My edf and tdf files are attached here. I have 27 individuals and 7 of them have been recaptured. There are three sampling occasions in the dataset.

I tried to model behavior (D~1,p0~b,sig~1), but got the following error message:

In sqrt(diag(solve(myfit$hessian))) : NaNs produced

> mb
 Model:  D ~ 1 p0 ~ b sig ~ 1
 Run time:  8.027167  minutes
 AIC:  341.5535

Summary table:
                Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)
p0.(Intercept)    -1.825 0.493 -3.700   0.000
p.behav          -20.998   NaN    NaN     NaN
sig.(Intercept)    5.142 0.163 31.634   0.000
d0.(Intercept)    -2.069 0.275 -7.527   0.000
psi.constant       0.223 0.387  0.576   0.565
*Density intercept is log(individuals per pixel)
  Nhat(state-space) = exp(d0.)*nrow(ssDF)
  (caution is warranted when model contains density covariates)

So does this mean that this can't be run? And if so, why is this?

Thanks for your time,

Jenni Poutanen

PhD student

Section of Ecology

Biology Department

University of Turku, Finland

messages.subject: Re: Modelling behavioral response
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jenni,

The p.behav coefficient is for a trap-specific behavioral response, so the model is indicating that capture probability essentially goes to zero for a given individual at a given trap after initial capture.  The problem is that you did not observe an individual recaptured in the same trap.  I'm not sure there is a great fix for this.  If the behavioral response is real, you'd want to keep it in the model to adjust p0 (and subsequently, d0).  But the coefficient will have a nonsense estimate because of the link scale conversion of Pr(y = 1) = 0, which is negative infinity.

What kind of traps were used?  If they were live-capture traps, you'd want to make sure the multinomial model (multicatch = T) is used.

messages.subject: Improving processing time for discrete space modelling?
messages.subject_clean: Improving processing time for discrete space modelling?
messages.body_plain:
Hi group,

Rookie SCR modeler here. I've switched over from JAGS to oSCR to help deal with the computation time for SCR modelling over a discrete state space with camera trap data, but I'm still finding that my run times for even the most basic models in oSCR take a very long time. I'm not sure if this is due to the nature of my dataset or if there's an error in my model structure that I'm missing.

I'm working with a very reduced dataset - using a subset with 8 individuals, 40 cameras, and 30 occasions (days), whereas the full dataset uses 103 cameras and over a year of trap-days. However, even with this reduced dataset, the null model (D~1, p0~1, sigma~1) takes 58 minutes to run. When I use the full dataset the null model takes over 2 days to run. I just thought it would be running much faster so this seems a little weird to me. It's occurred to me that this might be because I have a large number of pixels in the state space (11550), but as it's already at a resolution of 250m * 250m, I'm reluctant to go coarser than that for the purposes of this project.

Anyway, eventually I'll need to be using the full dataset doing a model selection process with up to 6 spatial covariates. Given the current state of things it's looking like this could take forever to accomplish, which isn't the end of the world, but any thoughts or suggestions on improving processing time would be very much appreciated! Or if anyone is able to spot an error in the structure that I may have missed.

The scrFrame is summarized below, and the EDF and TDF for this subset are attached.

str(sf3)

>   ..$ session: Factor w/ 1 level "1": 1 1
>   ..$ sex    : Factor w/ 2 levels "female","male": 1 2

>   ..$ : int [1:40, 1:30] 1 1 1 1 0 0 0 0 1 0 ...
>   .. ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
>   .. .. ..$ : NULL
>   .. .. ..$ : chr [1:30] "90" "91" "92" "93" ...
>  $ occasions    : int 30
>  $ type         : chr "scr"
>  $ mmdm         : num 3.62
>  $ mdm          : num 4.38
>  $ telemetry    : NULL
>  - attr(*, "class")= chr "scrFrame"

My null model is written as:

> #equal to SCR0
> out1.0 <- oSCR.fit(scrFrame=sf3,ssDF=ssDF,DorN="N",encmod="B",
>                    model=list(D~1,p0~1,sigma~1))

*As a side note, I'm not sure if it matters that I've characterized this as binomial encounter model rather than Poisson. As it happens, my encounter data is such that no individual was seen at any location more than once on the same occasion, so while I guess it is technically count data, it more closely resembles presence/absence data. If anyone has a thought on this choice I'd happily take pointers!

Thanks very much for any advice! These SCR help forums really have been life saving.

Cheers,

Nina

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nina,

Try the following script with the changes I made. Looks like it gets done in under a minute. Also, I tried with DorN = D (Poisson model) and N (binomial model), and they both were quick. I bet its that 4th column. I have to admit, the binomial model probably needs some work, its not as up to date/as well tested as the Poisson model. Also, make sure you have the most recent version of the package (you can do that using the first few lines of code)

Hope this helps!!! 😊

install.packages("githubinstall")

install.packages("devtools")

library(githubinstall)

library(devtools)

#install oSCR directly from github

install_github("jaroyle/oSCR")

#load oSCR

library(oSCR)

edf <- read.csv("CV_grid_edf2_subset.csv")

#need to make day 90 occasion 1 - some sausage making:

days2occasion <- data.frame(day=90:119, occasion=1:length(90:119))

edf2 <- merge(edf,days2occasion,by="day",all.x=T, all.y = F)

head(edf2)

tdf <- read.csv("CV_grid_tdf_subset.csv")

head(tdf)

#remove the pixel ID column so its < ID X Y opperation1:K >

tdf <- tdf[,-4]

sf <- data2oscr(edf = edf2,

                sess.col = 2,

                id.col = 3,

                occ.col = 5,

                trap.col = 4,

                tdf = list(tdf),

                K = 30,

                ntraps = nrow(tdf))$scrFrame

ss <- make.ssDF(sf,buffer = 4, res=0.5)

par(mfrow=c(1,2))

plot(sf)

plot(ss,sf)

#set trimS to the same value as the buffer to speecd things up

system.time(m0 <- oSCR.fit(scrFrame=sf,ssDF=ss, trimS=4))

#  user  system elapsed

messages.subject: VS: Modelling behavioral response
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thanks for your replies.

Yes we don't have recaptures at the same trap. In this dataset we used non-invasive DNA sampling, which should also minimize the behavioral response. But we have also data with trail cameras, which could cause some behavioral effect (this species seem to be very interested in cameras so they might have an attractive effect). So good to know why the effect couldn't be modelled here, if the same problem occurs with another dataset.

best regards,
Jenni
